title: Cross-system UI guidance
summary: Operational rules for Material on Android, Fluent on Microsoft platforms, Carbon for enterprise density, and keeping the product design system in charge. Each rule links the page for that system.

rules.title: Material patterns
rules.intent: Use Material 3 when the experience should align with Android, and theme it instead of pasting the default Google look onto another brand
principles: On Android, follow Material layout breakpoints (the former window size classes) and change panes, navigation, and actions as the window grows
Implement Android UI with Jetpack Compose, the toolkit Material currently recommends. Views remain available for maintenance, not for new Material features
Express brand through Material tokens. Reference, system, and component tokens are the customization path, not a one-off restyle of each component
antiPatterns: Using Material rules blindly in any brand
A compact phone layout stretched unchanged onto an expanded window
acceptance: The decision to use Material is written down, with the target platform
Layout changes are mapped to compact, medium, expanded, large, and extra-large breakpoints
limitations: Breakpoints apply to Android and the web Material guidance. They do not replace a product design system that is not Material
Component specs stay on the component pages. This rule does not copy sizes

rules.title: Fluent patterns
rules.intent: Use Fluent 2 for Microsoft-oriented products, and let the layout follow the platform instead of a phone metaphor
principles: Make the layout feel natural on the platform: adapt to the screen, and reuse native platform components for ordinary UI
Use Fluent layout: a grid, spacing that groups related items, and a hierarchy that keeps the next decision comfortable
For a native Windows app, check the Windows app design docs alongside Fluent 2. Fluent's web pages are not the Windows control spec
antiPatterns: Forcing phone metaphors into desktop tools
Hardcoded pixels and hex values where a Fluent token already names the role
acceptance: Desktop controls follow Fluent or Windows conventions for the target shell
The layout still works when the window is resized, not only at one laptop width
limitations: Fluent 2 design principles and layout were checked. Windows control metrics stay on learn.microsoft.com and are not copied here

rules.title: Carbon enterprise patterns
rules.intent: Use Carbon as the reference for dense enterprise data, with spacing and table sizes chosen on purpose
principles: Use the Carbon spacing scale inside and between components. Density is allowed in a section. The whole page still needs space for the eye to rest
Put a data table in the main content, wide enough to avoid truncation, and pick one row size (extra small through extra large) for both header and body
Do not nest a table inside a table or a container so small that the data must be clipped
antiPatterns: Inventing ad hoc patterns for tables
Mixing row heights between the header and the body
acceptance: Enterprise tasks are reviewed against Carbon table and spacing guidance
The chosen density is named (xs, sm, md, lg, or xl) and used consistently
limitations: Row heights and spacing tokens change with Carbon versions. Read the linked pages for the current numbers. This rule does not freeze them

rules.title: Project DS authority
rules.intent: When the product already has tokens and components, those win over the default look of Material, Fluent, or Carbon
principles: Theme a chosen system through its own tokens: Material system tokens, Fluent alias tokens, or Carbon theme tokens
Change shared token values, not one-off overrides on individual components
Keep one visual system in the product. Do not combine Material, Fluent, and Carbon component looks in the same app
antiPatterns: Mixing 3 design systems in one app
Restyling a Carbon or Material component locally while the product tokens say something else
acceptance: Project conventions and token names are preserved
Any borrowed component is mapped onto the product's tokens, or the exception is written down
limitations: None of the three systems forbids using another system. The single-system rule is operational guidance for a product that already has an identity
Token pages describe each system's theming. They do not authorize replacing the repository's design system
